title: Multi-Agent Systems — Coordinate Through Explicit State
key_insight: An orchestrator or state machine assigns tasks and stores structured status, artifacts, and dependencies. Handoffs use typed results rather than vague prose.
body:
## Coordinate Through Explicit State

Agents pass long conversational messages and lose track of which steps are complete. Shared work needs a clearer record.

An orchestrator or state machine assigns tasks and stores structured status, artifacts, and dependencies. Handoffs use typed results rather than vague prose.

Set limits on turns, tokens, tools, and time. Detect repeated states so a disagreement cannot loop forever.
common_mistakes: Adding more agents always improves every task.
Conversational memory replaces structured workflow state.
Every agent should receive all available permissions.
mini_exercise: Draw “Coordinate Through Explicit State” as three labeled steps, then explain the decision at each step.
real_world_usage: Multiple model-driven workers can help on decomposable work, but coordination can add cost, delay, and new failure modes.
explain_back_prompt: Using “Coordinate Through Explicit State,” explain Multi-Agent Systems without assuming the listener knows AI engineering.

build_task.title: Design a bounded two-role workflow
build_task.context: Turn Multi-Agent Systems into one small, inspectable artifact.
steps: Choose a task with two genuinely distinct roles.
Define each role’s inputs and output schema.
Add a coordinator and stop rules.
build_task.expected_output: A versioned artifact with visible decisions, evidence, and failure handling.
build_task.hint: Keep the scope bounded and record why each decision was made.
